minutes.headline: Personnel Committee approved a revised civilian traffic job description and hired a facilities director at step five, grade 16.
minutes.summary: The committee approved the civilian traffic member job description revision, which opens the role to active public safety staff, then heard the HR consultant's progress update on the classification and pay study. It then approved the recommended starting step for the new facilities director and adjourned. Questions about the facilities director's budget and the consultant's timeline were discussed but not settled.

budget_items.what_was_said: Personnel manager recommended starting the new facilities director at step five based on his project management and construction coordination experience.
Members asked what budget the new position has; it was said a budget was carved out of the DPW budget when town meeting approved the position, including landscaping, but no figures were available.
Consultant said the town must decide where to sit in the market and how steps are structured, and will recommend two pay plan models.

decisions.decision: Consultant to deliver draft job descriptions by January 20th, with a draft pay plan for the non-bargained positions moved up to February 6th, ahead of the committee's meeting, and a draft report on February 15th.
Facilities director tentative start date of the 23rd, with appointment by the Select Board on the 17th.
Personnel manager will request the facilities budget details from Heather.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee voted to hire the new facilities director at step five of grade 16, on the Personnel manager's recommendation.
The committee approved a revised civilian traffic member job description, passing on a roll call in which some votes were only partly audible.
The HR consultant gave a progress update on the classification and pay study, with draft job descriptions due January 20th and a draft report February 15th.
Members asked what budget the facilities director position has; it was said a budget was carved out of the DPW budget, but no figures were available.

why_it_matters: The facilities director's pay is set by a step recommendation, and the position's budget was not stated at the meeting, so residents cannot yet see how it is funded from the DPW budget, which is paid mostly by taxes.
The classification and pay study will produce a new pay plan for non-bargained town positions, which sets what the town pays staff in future budgets.
watch_next: Consultant's draft job descriptions due January 20th, a draft pay plan February 6th, and a draft report February 15th.
Select Board appointment of the facilities director on the 17th, and the Personnel manager's request to Heather for the facilities budget details.
